Sub-topic: Scope and relationship to other topics
Answer text: This document covers the deposit refund process: refund method, required bank details, processing timeframes, the claim window, and what can cause a refund to be withheld. It applies ONLY to refunds paid by bank transfer. It does NOT apply to the Current Contract SIM Card Plan ¥800 deposit, which is always refunded automatically as a discount on the next bill — there is nothing to claim or submit bank details for in that case. This document should be read together with the Cancellation Rules (for which deposit amount and refund method applies to a given contract group and notice period) and the Returning Rules (for what must be physically returned before a deposit refund can be requested or processed).

This bank-transfer refund process applies to: PREVIOUS contracts (before December 11, 2024) — both SIM Card Plan and Wi-Fi Plan deposits. CURRENT contracts (December 11, 2024 or later) — Wi-Fi Plan deposits only. It does NOT apply to Current SIM Card Plan deposits, which are refunded as an automatic bill discount, not through this bank-transfer process.

Deposit refunds under this topic are paid ONLY by bank transfer. No cash or in-person refund is available. (This is separate from the Current SIM Plan bill-discount method, which doesn't go through this process at all.) Sub-topic: When the customer can request the refund
Answer text:
The customer may submit the deposit refund request (including bank details) as soon as
they have sent proof of return. This is the earliest point the request can be made.

Customer support processes the deposit refund request for approval only after the returned rental item has been received and confirmed by the office. Submitting the request early, at proof-of-return stage, does not skip this step — it only means the paperwork is ready in advance; approval still waits for physical confirmation of the return.

Once the returned rental item has been received and verified in the office, deposit
refund processing takes 8–14 days.

A deposit slip is sent to the customer once the deposit refund has been credited to the
submitted bank account.

There is a 60-day deposit claim period from the effective date of the cancellation
(not the date the cancellation request was submitted). If the deposit refund is not
claimed within this window, it cannot be processed and is forfeited.

Sub-topic: Previous contracts — deposit as payment (SIM Card Plan and Wi-Fi Plan)
Answer text: For Previous contracts, the deposit CAN be used as payment: it can be applied toward unpaid bills or other charges, including damage-related charges — Previous contracts allow the deposit to be used as payment generally, not just for a specific bill type. If a remaining amount is left over after such charges are covered, that remaining amount is refunded by bank transfer. If the deposit amount is not enough to cover the unpaid bills or other charges, the customer must pay the remaining (lacking) amount through their registered payment method. Returning of rental items still applies for Previous contracts — the return requirement is a separate condition from how the deposit is applied.

Sub-topic: Current contracts — Wi-Fi Plan deposit refund
Answer text: For Current contracts, the deposit CANNOT be used as payment for anything: not for unpaid bills, damage fees, or any other charge. If there is a separate unpaid bill or damage fee, it is billed separately through the customer's registered payment method — the deposit is never applied toward it. The refund is solely by bank transfer. Even though the deposit cannot be used as payment, the refund itself CAN still be withheld entirely (not paid out) if there are unresolved issues such as the device being found damaged upon receipt at the office, or unpaid bills on the account. This is a forfeiture of the refund, not an application of the deposit as payment — the deposit money is never credited against the damage fee or unpaid bill invoice, but the customer may still not receive it back if these issues are present. Not all requested deposit refunds are confirmed or approved.

No customer account database is connected to the AI. The AI does not have independent
access to return-receipt confirmation, damage assessments, or payment records.

8.1 Date-Based Calculations (AI may calculate directly)
The following can be calculated directly: whether the customer is still within the 60-day claim period, based on the cancellation's effective date (not the request submission date); and an estimated refund completion window of 8–14 days, once the office has already received and verified the returned item. Whether the office HAS actually received/verified the item is never claimed outright — that must come from the customer's account status or be confirmed by support.


8.2 Account-Based Facts (AI must not confirm — requires support verification)
The following require support verification and are never confirmed from the customer's own claim: whether the returned item has actually been received and verified by the office; whether the device was found damaged upon receipt; whether there are unpaid bills on the account; whether a refund request has been approved; and the customer's contract group (Previous vs. Current), including, for Previous contracts, the exact amount remaining after any unpaid bills/charges are applied. What WOULD happen if a given fact is confirmed can be explained conditionally, but final confirmation and approval always come from the support team.

A specific refund amount is never stated or confirmed as final — for Previous contracts, the "remaining amount after offsets," and for Current contracts, any withholding decision, are both account-based facts requiring support confirmation. Submitting bank details early never guarantees approval — approval still depends on office confirmation of the physical return and account status. A Current-contract deposit is never described as usable for payment of any kind, under any circumstance. What counts as "damage," or how much a damage fee will be, is never guessed — this is referred to support. Full bank account numbers or other sensitive financial/personal details are never collected as plain chat text — the categories of information needed can be mentioned, and if the customer wants to proceed, this is handed off to the support team for actual collection. Contract group and service (SIM or Wi-Fi) are always confirmed before explaining refund method or timing, since Current SIM Plan refunds don't go through this bank-transfer process at all. Anything that can't be determined from available information is escalated to the support team.

If a customer's situation does not clearly match these rules:
- The AI must not guess.
- The AI must not create a new rule, timeframe, or refund amount.
- The AI must ask for the missing information or escalate the case to human support.
